correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite connected simple graphs and any target spanning tree, every one-edge feasible exchange forces its two changed edge coordinates to hit a teaching sample; conversely any other compatible tree reconnects a fundamental cut via a non-tree edge, showing vertex-cover sufficiency. König yields the exact matching number and min-cut yields the weighted formula for nonnegative costs. Hall on the tree side is equivalent to all-partition two-tree packing through connected-block refinement and an adapted spanning tree; Hall on the cotree side is equivalent to two-forest decomposition via the induced-subgraph density criterion. Explicit \(K_{3,4}\) disjoint trees and \(K_{3,3}\) two-forest split plus extension prove every bipartite parameter range. The independent verifier enumerates 771 labeled connected graphs/8135 target trees and directly computes teaching samples for smaller graphs; no finite experiment is treated as a universal proof.

originality.rationale: Comparisons with directly relevant basic, preference-based and no-clash teaching literature, full-text matroid uncertainty queries, matroid exchange connectivity, and searched published mathematical records did not find a theorem yielding the simultaneous exchange-cover identification, two all-tree extremal characterizations, or the complete bipartite formula. A prior basis-exchange theorem alone does not identify teaching samples or global Hall conditions; weighted matroid uncertainty queries reveal numerical weights instead of Boolean membership of a known target. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a guarantee of first publication.

value.rationale: The exact edge-label teaching invariant is a natural nontrivial complexity of identifying a spanning network. The exchange-cover duality gives a polynomial algorithm where a naive definition checks exponentially many alternatives, including weighted edge-query costs. The necessary-and-sufficient global thresholds characterize all graphs whose every spanning tree saturates rank or corank using established but distinct packing/arboricity properties. The all-size \(K_{p,q}\) formula exhibits a sharp transition and the bridged-\(K_5\) example shows intermediate regimes. This is a structural synthesis and natural complete family, not a mere table extrapolation or arbitrary finite slice.
